lines.text: The fire spits. Something out past the light spits back.
I'll take first watch.
You took first watch last time. And you were asleep when I woke.
I was listening with my eyes shut.
What's in the stew?
Meat.
What kind?
Eat it while it's warm, {a}.
There are more stars here than at home.
Those aren't stars. Don't count them. They notice when you count them.
If I don't come back, burn my letters. Don't read them first.
What's in them?
Names. Just names.
Do you remember the way we came?
Yes.
So do I. It's just that it's not there any more.
Far off, someone is singing a lullaby in a voice that is almost right.
Don't answer it.
I wasn't going to.
You were humming along.
My boots are full of something.
Water?
It's warm.
Do you think the old gods can see us here?
I think something can. I've stopped hoping it's them.
Found a coin on the path. My grandfather's face is on it.
Your grandfather was a farmer.
I know.
Sleep in your armor tonight.
It chafes.
So do teeth.
Say my name, {b}.
Good. Say it again in the morning. Make sure it's still the same.
Two shadows sit on the far side of the fire. Two Scions sit on this side.
How many of us are there?
Don't look round.
The Pact feeds us, arms us, buries us. What do we owe it?
Everything. That was the price of the bread.
I dreamed of the Gate last night. It was breathing.
Mine too.
It was breathing in.
One Scion, one fire, and the long dark.
It's quiet. I wish it weren't. In the quiet I can hear how far home is.
I've started talking to the fire. It's better company than the trees.
The fire crackles, as if it had something to add.
One. Just one. If I keep saying it, nothing out there will think there are more of me to eat.
Hold still. This needs stitching.
Use the black thread.
Why?
So the blood doesn't show when I go home.
It doesn't hurt. That's what worries me.
Where?
Everywhere I can't feel.
If I can't walk tomorrow, leave me.
No.
Leave me with a knife, then. It's a kindness, {b}. For whatever finds me.
Do I look like myself to you?
Mostly.
Which part doesn't?
Get some sleep, {a}.
{a} keeps looking at their hands, turning them over, counting fingers.
Ten?
This time.
It knows my name, {b}. It said it from inside the tree.
Then don't give it any more. Not your House, not your mother's name. Nothing.
To {fallen}.
To {fallen}. The Chronicle will say it was quick.
Was it?
The Chronicle will say it was.
{fallen} had a ring. Should we take it home?
Leave it. The dark here keeps what it's given. Better it has the ring than us.
Someone has set out a bowl for {fallen} out of habit. Nobody takes it away.
If House {house_b} had held the line, {fallen} would be here.
Say that again in the town square, {a}. I'd like the Houses to hear it.
I hear {lost} calling. Off to the left, past the trees.
We all hear it. It isn't {lost}. Not any more.
We'll come back for {lost}.
Will we?
The Houses will put it to a vote.
No one talks much tonight. Everyone can hear it breathing, somewhere ahead.
If I fall tomorrow, my blade goes to House {house_a}. Not the Pact. My House.
Noted.
Swear it, {b}.
Tomorrow. Front line holds. Back line keeps us breathing.
And if the front line breaks?
Then the back line becomes the front line. Sleep.
Who do we pray to, out here?
Whoever's listening.
That's what I'm afraid of.
First night out. It's not so bad.
Wait.
Three rules. Don't follow lights. Don't answer your name unless one of us says it. Don't eat anything that's already cooked.
Who cooks things out here?
Rule three.
The map ends here.
The map ends wherever the last cartographer stopped walking.
Your House owes mine forty Gold, {b}.
Then you'd better hope I live to pay it.
Did your House send you to watch me, {a}?
Did yours?
Neither answers. Both keep their hands where the other can see them.
For a {house_b}, you swing well.
For a {house_a}, you bleed quietly. I'll take that as a compliment.
They say House {house_b} made a bargain with something under the Gate.
They say a lot of things about House {house_a}, too. Some of them are even about the dead ones.
When we're home, come and drink at our hall. We pay better than {house_a}.
Ask me again when you've buried as many as we have.
Remember the old hall, {b}? The long table?
Half the seats are empty now.
Then we'll fill them. That's what we're out here for.
Your father would be proud.
My father told me never to go through the Gate.
Then he'd be proud and furious. Both. Like always.
Whatever happens tomorrow, House {house_a} comes home with something.
Even if it's only our names.
If we fail, what happens to the town?
Don't.
I want to know.
Then you shouldn't have asked to come.
They say the bells at home ring every hour the party is gone. Out here, you can almost hear them.
Is it always like this? The shaking, after?
No. After a while you stop shaking. That's worse.
My knees know the weather before the sky does. They say it's going to rain blood.
They said that last time.
And?
How many times have you been through the Gate, {a}?
Enough that it waves.
Do you ever take that armor off?
Not out here. Out here it's the only thing that remembers what I swore.
I've had seven sergeants. I've buried six.
And the seventh?
Still owes me money.
Where did you get that bread?
Where did you leave it?
Eat. You're welcome.
I drew the cards for tomorrow.
And?
I drew them again.
And?
I'm not going to draw them a third time.
What are our odds?
Better than yesterday. Worse than you'd like. Want to bet on it?
Your hands are humming, {a}.
They do that near old places. Something here used to be a spell. A big one.
What did it do?
I think it ended something.
{a} soaks split knuckles in the stream. The water turns pink, then black.
Should it do that?
Probably not.
Sing something.
Not here. Things out here learn the tunes.
Found a gear in a wolf's stomach. Fine work. Older than the kingdom.
Throw it away.
It's still turning.
You twitch in your sleep, {a}. Like something trying to get out.
Not trying. Waiting.
{a} draws a circle around the camp in salt and ash.
Will it keep them out?
It will tell me when they come in.
Your summoned thing is staring at me.
It does that. It's deciding whether you're food or furniture.
You were laughing, back there. When it bled.
Was I?
You still are.
My blade is quieter tonight.
Quieter?
It's had enough to drink.
Something howls. Then something answers it from much closer.
Beasts, only beasts.
Beasts don't use names, {a}. That one said yours.
The trees moved while I slept.
They do that.
Toward us.
The fire burns low and green. The water around the camp is very still.
Don't look in the water.
Why?
Because something in it is looking up.
The dead here are restless.
They're not restless. They're patient. There's a difference, and it's us.
I can't feel my fingers.
Count them, then.
Nine.
Count again.
It is warm here. Too warm. The fire is unnecessary, and burns anyway.
Smell that?
Brimstone and bread. Someone down there is baking.
Hammers. All night. I can hear hammers.
There's nobody left to hold them.
I know.
Someone waved to me from a window.
There are no windows in this street.
It waved anyway.
Bells at midnight. They're calling the faithful.
To what?
Supper.
Six altars. Six gods. Who do we thank for the fire?
Thank the one that's watching. Only one of them is.
The hills here are warm to the touch, and they rise and fall, very slowly.
Sleep lightly.
I wasn't planning to sleep at all.
The stars are wrong here.
There are no stars here, {a}.
Then what's that?
Nobody looks up again.
